fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Front Driveway; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Multiple Structures; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Terrain
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker visible from the road at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly.
• Mark the access drive entrance clearly so responders can distinguish it from neighboring driveways or field openings.
• Post visible signage or markers along the access drive indicating the direction and distance to the main residence.
• Trim any vegetation along the access drive that narrows the travel width or reduces visibility for responding vehicles.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles, equipment, and debris so responding units can reach all structures without repositioning.
• Mark a designated staging area near the main residence where emergency vehicles can park without blocking the single access point.
• Identify and mark a turnaround point on the property so large vehicles can reverse direction without entering soft or uneven ground.
• Trim vegetation growing against or overhanging the detached structures so responders can move around all sides of each building.
• Clear a walking path between the main residence and each detached structure so responders can move between buildings without obstruction.
• Keep gates, if present on the access drive, unlocked or secured with a combination known to local emergency services.
• Post the property address on each detached structure or mark each building with a visible identifier to help responders distinguish between them during an incident.

wildfire.conditions: Open Green Space; Grass Cover; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Tree Cluster; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Single Access Route; Grass Cover; Limited Rear Access; Scattered Shrubs
wildfire.recommendations:
• Mow or cut the grass across the open areas surrounding the structure to reduce the amount of dry ground fuel near the building.
• Trim back any shrubs that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Thin the scattered trees near the structure so branches do not connect or form a continuous path toward the building.
• Remove lower branches from trees in the cluster so fire cannot climb from the ground into the upper canopy near the structure.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so vehicles can move through without obstruction.
• Cut back vegetation along the sides and rear of the property to open up movement and visibility around the structure.
• Keep grass along the driveway edges mowed short to reduce the chance of fire spreading quickly toward the structure along that corridor.
• Clear any dead or dry plant material from beneath trees and shrubs near the building.
